newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan March forex reserves up to US$88.789 bln.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan March forex reserves up to US$88.789 bln.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign exchange reserves rose to US$88.789 billion at the end of March from $88.63 billion at the end of February, the central bank said on Thursday.
The central bank, which announced the figure in a surprised move, did not give a reason for the rise.
The bank had been scheduled to announce the end-March foreign exchange reserves figure on Friday at noon.

Taiwan's foreign exchange reserves, the world's third largest after Japan's and China's, fell in late 1995 and early 1996 as political tensions with rival China intensified into a military crisis in March 1996, triggering heavy capital outflows.
The trend reversed after Taiwan's March 23, 1996 presidential election and an easing of tensions with China, rising slowly but steadily since April 1996.
Beijing held war games and missile tests in the Taiwan Strait in the run-up to the presidential poll, triggering waves of U.S. dollar buying and a run on gold.
The central bank intervened during the crisis to support the Taiwan dollar and the island's hypersensitive stock market.
Taiwan's foreign reserves peaked at $100.412 billion in June 1995, just before tensions with China erupted over President Lee Teng-hui's controversial private visit to the United States.
Note - Foreign currency reserves in billions of U.S. dollar.
